Frasers Property’s Capital Recycling: What It Means for FCT and FLCT
article:
Frasers Property Limited
(SGX: TQ5), or FPL, recently announced a
proposed optimisation
of approximately S$2.1 billion of hospitality assets, following its privatisation of Frasers Hospitality Trust (FHT) in 2025.
At first glance, investors may see this as a simple divestment.
However, the bigger story is about capital allocation, balance sheet optimisation, and long-term value creation.
While the transaction does not directly involve
Frasers Centrepoint Trust
(SGX: J69U.SI) or
Frasers Logistics & Commercial Trust
(SGX: BUOU), it provides clues about how FPL manages capital across its wider real estate platform.
Understanding the Hospitality Portfolio Optimisation
Rather than adopting a one-size-fits-all strategy, FPL reviewed every hospitality asset individually.
Under the plan, mature and lower-yielding stabilised assets will be fully divested to unlock capital.
Meanwhile, for assets with identifiable value-enhancement opportunities, FPL retains an effective 49.95% exposure through a co-investment structure.
Non-core assets are kept for future opportunistic divestment, while consolidating full ownership of Fraser Suites Singapore facilitates potential redevelopment of the wider Valley Point site.
This approach allows mature assets to be monetised while retaining exposure where active management can unlock additional upside.
Notably, the transaction is priced at approximately a 6.7% premium to the latest independent valuation and 1.6% above the implied take-private valuation level, reflecting disciplined execution.
FPL will continue to manage around S$4.2 billion of hospitality assets under management (AUM) post-transaction, preserving its recurring management fee income while operating a leaner capital structure.
What This Says About FPL
The proposed restructuring highlights active portfolio management over passive asset ownership.
On a pro forma basis, the deal is expected to reduce net gearing by 3.3 percentage points, while boosting earnings per share (EPS) by 3.4%, net asset value (NAV) per share by 1.3%, and return on equity (ROE) by 0.1 percentage points.
Crucially, FPL is not exiting hospitality; management intends to maintain scale and operational income through a more capital-efficient platform.
For unitholders of Frasers Centrepoint Trust (FCT) and Frasers Logistics & Commercial Trust (FLCT), sponsor quality and balance sheet strength matter greatly.
A financially stronger sponsor with lower debt is better equipped to support its
real estate investment trust (REIT)
ecosystem.
In 1HFY2026, FCT posted a 20.3% year-on-year (YoY) revenue surge to S$221.9 million on 99.8% retail occupancy, driven by the acquisition of Northpoint City South Wing in May 2025.
FPL’s ongoing capital recycling could eventually yield further high-quality pipeline opportunities for FCT down the road.
Similarly, FLCT delivered an 11.9% YoY increase in DPU before capital top-ups for 1HFY2026, supported by robust 96.1% portfolio occupancy and strong industrial demand.
With FLCT maintaining an aggregate leverage of 33.7%, a financially disciplined sponsor enhances overall flexibility for future growth initiatives across industrial, logistics, or commercial assets.
The Shift Toward a Platform-Led Model
This transaction reflects a broader evolution in real estate, where listed property groups increasingly generate value through capital recycling, asset management, co-investments, and fee generation rather than sole asset ownership.
Moving forward, investors should keep an eye on the upcoming Extraordinary General Meeting (EGM) for shareholder approval, progress on the Valley Point site redevelopment, and how FPL ultimately redeploys its freed-up capital.
Get Smart: The Story Isn’t About Selling Hotels
FPL’s announcement represents a broader shift towards disciplined capital allocation rather than a retreat from hospitality.
It demonstrates a clear willingness to recycle mature assets while retaining exposure to future growth opportunities through active co-investment and platform management.
For FCT and FLCT unitholders, watching sponsor strategy is critical.
Even when major restructuring moves do not directly involve their specific trusts,
a stronger, more flexible sponsor
provides a sturdier foundation for the entire ecosystem.
Ultimately, the strongest property platforms build long-term value not by simply holding the most assets, but by allocating capital where it can earn the highest risk-adjusted return.

title: All-Link Air & Sea to raise $20.1 mil comprising 37.9 mil offering shares for Mainboard IPO
article:
Logistics solutions provider All-Link Air & Sea Limited is seeking to raise $20.1 million for its Mainboard initial public offering (IPO).

The IPO of 37.9 million offering shares comprises 35.8 million placement shares and 2.1 million public offer shares priced at 53 cents apiece.

For the FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 ended December, All-Link’s revenue stood at US$4.8 million, US$71.5 million and US$74.1 million respectively. Earnings stood at US$1.2 million, US$8.4 million and US$6.3 million respectively.

In the three years, the company’s top five customers accounted for approximately 99.7%, 99.8% and 89.9% of its revenue respectively. The TikTok Group, in particular, accounted for 98% of All-Link’s total revenue in FY2024.

According to All-Link, it intends to use proceeds from the offering to expand its operations, conduct acquisitions, joint ventures (JVs) and alliances, invest in technology and digital capabilities, as well as pay airlines, carriers and co-loaders. Beyond issue expenses, the company will also use part of the proceeds for general expensese and working capital.

The public offer opens at 9pm on July 28 and will close at 12pm on Aug 3.

All-Link’s shares will commence trading on a “ready” basis on Aug 5.

CGS International Securities Singapore is the issue manager, underwriter and placement agent.

title: Singapore's AUM grew 10% in 2025 to $6.7 trillion
article:
In 2025, Singapore’s assets under management (AUM) grew by 10% to $6.7 trillion, or US$5.2 trillion at an exchange rate of $1.2841. Of this, traditional AUM grew by 9% y-o-y, and alternatives by 0.4%. 76% of AUM was sourced from outside Singapore, and 88% of total AUM is invested globally, outside of Singapore.

Discretionary AUM accounted for more than half of total AUM in 2025, reflecting the substance, expertise and value-adding nature of investment professionals based here, and Singapore’s ongoing attractiveness as a leading centre in APAC for investment and capital deployment.

Singapore’s net inflows grew by 29% y-o-y in 2025. This momentum is driven by a rise in new mandates acquired and managed from Singapore.

The 0.4% growth in alternative AUM was led by growth in hedge funds and REITs. AUM growth for Private Equity and Venture Capital fell last year as the entry of several new managers more than offset the downsizing of one large manager. Meanwhile, real estate AUM dipped further amidst compressed valuations and weaker investor sentiment.

As of Dec 31 2025, a total of 1,406 variable capital companies (VCCs) were incorporated or re-domiciled in Singapore for various use cases and fund strategies. These umbrella or standalone VCCs, representing 3,443 sub-funds, were managed by over 50% of regulated fund management companies in Singapore. The asset managers and investment community are supported by a strong network of legal and tax advisors and service providers for fund administration and governance, and a suite of Singapore corporate and legal structures including VCCs for investment management and fund domiciliation to be co-located.

In 2025, MAS introduced the Equity Market Development Programme (EQDP) to strengthen the local asset management and research ecosystem. Under this programme, MAS invests in fund strategies that invest fully or substantially in Singapore public equities managed by asset managers that demonstrate a strong track record and proven investment capabilities. These asset managers have also committed to growing their investment and research capabilities in Singapore.

See also: Ascend Asia Asset Management launches new credit investment strategy

The Exchange Traded Fund (ETF) Industry Taskforce co-led by MAS and the Singapore Exchange also worked with the asset management industry to support the growth of the ETF market and offer more choices to investors. During the year, MAS also continued with our Private Market Programme to anchor marquee managers in private equity, private credit and infrastructure in Singapore.

title: MAS and ABS establish AI-Driven Cyber and Technology Risk Taskforce
article:
The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS) announced the establishment of the AI-Driven Cyber and Technology Risk Taskforce (ACT) on July 28.

Bringing together members since May this year, the taskforce, an industry-wide initiative, seeks to strengthen collective cyber and technology resilience in response to emerging threats posed by artificial intelligence (AI).

“Frontier AI technology is reshaping the cyber threat landscape. Its ability to rapidly identify, exploit vulnerabilities and automate attacks at scale is a serious cause for concern for the financial sector,” reads the joint statement dated July 28. “Against this backdrop, coordinated sector-wide action is critical to strengthening the financial sector's resilience against the threat.”

The taskforce will focus on three areas: industry collaboration, capability uplift and guidance development.

Industry collaboration will see the financial services sector share AI cybersecurity use cases and experience. It will also support the engagement and collaboration wiith industry cybersecurity and AI experts.

The taskforce will also uplift the financial services industry’s knowledge of cyber defence and conduct proof-of-concept trials to “explore and validate” AI-enabled tools against the evolving threat landscape.

See also: DBS says its gen-AI enabled virtual assistants reach 10 million customers

Finally, the taskforce seeks to strengthen financial institutions’ cyber security posture by developing guidance on new measures, controls and solutions to better detect, prevent and respond to sophisticated AI-enabled threats.

“Frontier AI is increasing the severity, scale and sophistication of cyber threats,” says Vincent Loy, assistant managing director (technology) and chief technology officer at MAS. “The financial sector must respond with urgency and through strong collaboration. Through this taskforce, MAS will work closely with industry partners to strengthen our collective defences and ensure Singapore’s financial sector remains resilient against AI-enabled risks.”

“AI is reshaping the cyber threat landscape, and the financial sector must continue to move together to stay resilient,” adds Ong-Ang Ai Boon, director, ABS. “Through close coordination, strong governance and ongoing partnership with regulators and industry stakeholders, Singapore’s financial sector remains vigilant, agile and committed to strengthening cyber and technology resilience in the face of evolving AI-related risks and emerging technologies.”

The taskforce includes members from MAS, ABS, as well as the three banks - DBS, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation (OCBC) and United Overseas Bank (UOB). It also includes the Singapore Exchange (SGX), Network for Electronic Transfers (NETS), and Banking Computer Services (BCS).

title: ST Engineering wins $840 mil rail services contract in Taiwan
article:
ST Engineering has won a rail services contract worth $840 million to provide turnkey rail services for the Taoyuan MRT Brown Line in Taiwan.

The deal, won via its urban solutions unit, will expand ST Engineering’s role in Taiwan’s rail network where it has been active for over three decades.

Project execution is expected to commence in the fourth quarter of 2026 and will be delivered over eight years.

Under the contract, won as part of a consortium with Hyundai Rotem, ST Engineering will lead overall project management and systems integration for the project.

ST Engineering will also provide rail electronics solutions including supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA), communications system, automatic fare collection system and platform screen doors.

The company says it will be responsible for the overall integration and delivery of key project components, including the signalling system, track works and bulk substation building civil works.

See also: Ever Glory secures more than $168 mil in new contracts, lifts order book to above $1 bil

Hyundai Rotem, the consortium partner, will provide the rolling stock and power supply system.

“This contract reflects our customer’s confidence in our ability to deliver large-scale rail infrastructure projects, drawing on decades of experience in delivering major rail projects in Taiwan and around the world,” says Gareth Tang, president, urban solutions of ST Engineering.

“We look forward to supporting the continued expansion of Taoyuan's rail network, and delivering a world-class metro system that enhances accessibility for local communities,” he adds.

See also: Sanli Environmental wins $60.1 mil contract across private and public sectors

Comprising seven stations, the 11.38km Taoyuan MRT Brown Line links Taoyuan City and the Greater Taipei area.

This project adds to ST Engineering’s global track record of more than 200 rail projects across 50 cities worldwide, underscoring its capabilities in providing end-to-end rail solutions from project management and systems integration to rail electronics solutions.

ST Engineering shares closed at $10.53 on July 28, down 0.57% for the day but up 25.21% year to date.

title: Chinese luxury jeweller sheds US$2.1 bil on 66% growth outlook
article:
(July 28): Laopu Gold Co lost US$2.1 billion ($2.72 billion) in market value Tuesday after the Chinese jeweller flagged slowing sales, unsettling investors who had been betting on some of China’s most viral consumer brands.

The company’s Hong Kong-listed shares slid nearly 24% to HK$302.20 (US$38.50 or $49.82) at close, the most since the Beijing-based firm’s June 2024 listing. A day earlier, Laopu projected first-half 2026 revenue growth of 60% to 66%, reaching 20.5 billion yuan ($3.92 billion), with non-IFRS adjusted net profit rising 83% to 85%, to as much as 4.36 billion yuan.

Though still strong year on year, the outlook marks a sharp slowdown from the 251% revenue surge recorded in the same period last year and fell short of analysts’ expectations. Both Goldman Sachs Group Inc and Citigroup Inc cut their earnings forecasts following the update.

“The pronounced decline reflects Laopu’s high sensitivity to gold price swings, as consumers prefer weight-based products over fixed-priced ones in a downcycle,” Morningstar Inc analyst Jeff Zhang wrote in a note.

Laopu’s deceleration mirrors a broader cooling across China’s once-“viral” consumer brands — from makers of collectible toys like Labubu to beverage chain Chagee — which surged on speculative buying and social-media hype before demand normalised. For Laopu, the retreat in gold prices has accelerated that shift away from the explosive growth it enjoyed over the past two years.

Gold prices have fallen about 25% from a record high in January, weighing on consumer appetite for jewellery as a store of value.

See also: China’s Fang Xinghai probe pushes finance cases to over 400

The preliminary figures implied net profit in the second quarter was about 30% below estimates, Citigroup analysts including Tiffany Feng wrote in a note, while cutting their net-profit estimates for 2026 to 2028. Goldman Sachs also trimmed its profit estimates for the same period, as well as price target for Laopu to HK$560 from HK$650.

To stimulate sales, Laopu plans to offer more attractive pricing through incremental discounts and new products with lower price per gram, Citigroup said in the note, citing Laopu’s management.

Still, Laopu’s overall first-half growth remains strong relative to other domestic jewellers and western luxury brands. That’s mainly due to what the company described as “the continuous expansion of brand influence” and “the improvement in high-value customer consumption”.

See also: Trip.com fined in China antitrust case as price wars continue

Unlike traditional Chinese jewellers, which price many items largely by weight and prevailing gold prices, Laopu sells most of its products at fixed prices that emphasise craftsmanship and brand value. Its pieces now command a hefty premium over the underlying value of gold.

title: MSCI CEO tells investors ignoring climate risk, ‘you only have yourself to blame’
article:
(JUly 28): As temperatures continue their relentless rise, most investors are still ignoring the impact of a hotter planet on asset values, according to Henry Fernandez, the chief executive of MSCI Inc.

The tendency is understandable, given investors are generally focused on short-term issues, he said. But “the climate is still changing, the world is still overheating, agricultural productivity is declining and there is an impact on companies,” Fernandez said in an interview in London.

Rising temperatures are now “a source of risk and return in any investment you have, and if you ignore this risk you only have yourself to blame,” he said.

The comments come as Europe endures record heat, triggering massive wildfires and disrupting life across the continent. This summer’s heat has been exacerbated by the impact of a powerful El Niño, driving temperatures even higher and threatening food production amid severe droughts. ING’s chief economist Carsten Brzeski has called the string of heat waves a “wake-up call,” noting that the thermometer is now a leading indicator for analysts to monitor.

As wildfires engulf large parts of France and Spain, more than 300,000 people have had to flee their homes, which US climate scientist Daniel Swain notes is roughly equivalent to the number of people evacuated from Dunkirk during WWII.

“Widespread, though yet untold, structure loss appears to have occurred,” he said in a post on X.

See also: STI can reach 6,800 because of ‘Orchard Road effect’: Maybank Securities

MSCI, which is among the world’s biggest providers of market indexes, is now actively expanding its palette of products to meet the moment. Last month, it acquired First Street, a specialist in climate risk data and analytics, for US$120 million ($155.1 million). The deal gives it access to physical climate-risk data for 2.4 billion assets, adding to the roughly four million assets such as manufacturing plants and warehouses that MSCI already tracked.

The acquisition is intended to help MSCI and its clients prepare for the hit asset valuations face as “climate-related physical risks accelerate globally,” the company said in June.

The corporations that make up major stock indexes are already voicing their concerns. An analysis by BloombergNEF found that major companies mentioned extreme heat a record number of times in their latest quarterly filings, indicating that they increasingly recognise the operational and financial risks posed by rising temperatures.

See also: Standard Chartered calls time on the de-dollarisation trade

The impacts of global warming are set to intensify in the years ahead, as the planet’s baseline temperature continues to rise, scientists have warned.

The world briefly surpassed the critical 1.5C global warming threshold for the first time back in 2024. The temperature is now on track to rise by almost twice that level this century, a trajectory scientists have called catastrophic.

In North America, severe heat waves now occur twice as often as they did in the middle of the 20th century, which a growing number of academic studies shows are costing the country billions of dollars in economic growth. Europe, however, stands out as the world’s fastest-warming continent.

Allianz SE, Europe’s largest primary insurer, recently published heat-impact simulations showing that Germany, the biggest EU economy, may face losses through 2030 of about US$130 billion. For France, the amount is US$240 billion. Sectors most at risk include infrastructure, food and health, the analysis found.

At the same time, efforts to curb the rising emissions that contribute to higher temperatures have suffered setbacks. The European Commission this month recommended delaying penalties on energy importers that don’t comply with the bloc’s methane rules. It has also proposed a slower pace of reductions to the EU’s emissions cap on its carbon market. In the US, President Donald Trump has unwound Biden-era policies that supported solar, wind and electric vehicles.

Fernandez said MSCI’s decision to emphasise the importance of climate change for investors is not about “making any judgment of any values.”

But when it comes to the issue of climate change and sustainable investing, “there is a lot of politics and ideology,” he said.

title: Korean markets hit by turmoil as chip rout forces trading halts
article:
(July 28): South Korean stocks suffered a series of trading suspension on Tuesday, as a sell-off in chipmakers spread across sectors.

The benchmark Kospi Index plunged nearly 11%, with Samsung Electronics Co and SK Hynix Inc tumbling over 13% each. The Korea Exchange halted cash trading in both the Kospi and Kosdaq gauges for 20 minutes each, after earlier suspending programme trades as futures plunged.

A bellwether of the popular artificial intelligence (AI) trade, the Korean market has rapidly turned into a cautionary tale on the perils of excessive investor fervour. The Kospi has fallen more than 30% from its peak about a month ago, pressured by periodic concerns over major global AI firms’ ability to turn high spending into profit and intensifying competition from Chinese rivals.

“Sentiment toward Korean semiconductor stocks is extremely weak,” said Ha SeokKeun, chief investment officer at Eugene Asset Management. “Broad risk-off, forced deleveraging, widening hyperscaler CDS spreads, and deteriorating retail investor sentiment are all adding to the selling pressure.”

Of the 14 circuit-breaker trading halts triggered on the Kospi since 2000 — a relatively rare form of intervention adopted at times of turmoil including the Covid pandemic and the Iran war — eight have occurred this year.

See also: Big Asia stock funds turn to laggards to cut risk from AI swings

The Kospi had been the world’s best-performing stock gauge earlier, up more than 100% this year at its peak. But the US$4 trillion ($5.17 trillion) market’s rapid ascension has come with bouts of wild swings, with its 30-day volatility at an all-time high.

Thinning liquidity has also turned the market even more volatile. Kospi’s traded value was more than 30% below the past 30-day average in mid afternoon trading.

The sell-off is set to inflict more pain on the Asian country’s retail investors, who have flocked to leveraged exchange-traded funds tracking chip stocks launched at near peak price levels in late May. Most of the products have lost around 60% or more since their debut.

See also: Adidas shares edge out Nike even before World Cup final

Foreign investors offloaded five trillion won (US$3.4 billion or $4.4 billion) of Kospi shares, while retail traders added. Focus is also on SK Hynix’s earnings due Wednesday.

Tuesday’s sell-off followed declines in global semiconductor stocks in the previous session, aggravated by reported progress by a Chinese state-backed company on mass producing certain chipmaking machines.

“Coupled with reports of domestic DUV lithography adoption, China’s semiconductor self-sufficiency is delivering tangible milestones,” said Jason Minsang Kam, head of active equity management at Kyobo Life Insurance Co. “This has triggered fears of a potential ‘bloodbath’ in commodity memory through supply gluts.”

title: DBS says its gen-AI enabled virtual assistants reach 10 million customers
article:
DBS has rolled out DBS Joy for corporate customers and DBS digibot for individual customers, bringing Generative AI and agentic AI capabilities to more than 10 million users across Singapore, Hong Kong and Taiwan.

Earlier this week, DBS Joy became fully agentic in Singapore, enabling corporate and SME customers to go beyond asking questions to completing simple banking tasks through a single conversation.

Meanwhile, DBS digibot has been enhanced with Gen AI capabilities across Singapore, Hong Kong and Taiwan since earlier this year, with new wealth-related conversational capabilities to be introduced from next week. In a subsequent phase, DBS digibot will be further enhanced with agentic AI capabilities, enabling customers to complete common servicing tasks such as checking card usage, tracking rewards points, and blocking or replacing cards.

The agentic capabilities for both virtual assistants will be activated only after customers log in to DBS IDEAL or DBS/POSB digibank, with the AI acting solely on instructions initiated by authenticated customers.

The virtual assistants are expected to handle more than one million chats monthly, helping customers get answers faster and complete everyday banking tasks more seamlessly. Customer support remains accessible to those who prefer to speak with a customer service officer for their more complex needs.

Said DBS Group Chief Operating Officer Derrick Goh, “The true value of AI lies in delivering meaningful outcomes for customers at scale. Today, DBS Joy and DBS digibot serve more than 10 million customers across the region, enabling us to bring Gen AI and agentic AI into everyday banking interactions. Building on more than a decade of AI innovation, we are taking the next leap forward – moving from helping customers find information to helping them get things done. This is especially significant in corporate banking, where digital assistants remain uncommon and agentic capabilities even more so. By combining our deep digital capabilities, trusted customer relationships and proprietary AI platforms, we are reimagining how banking services are delivered.”

title: Man Group assets hit all time high after bumper first half
article:
(July 28): Man Group Plc hit a 16-year high after the company’s assets jumped to a record in the first half of the year as clients poured money into the firm’s long-only investment strategies and strong performance gains helped drive growth.

Assets under management at the world’s largest listed hedge fund firm soared to US$253.6 billion ($327.8 billion) in the first half of the year, according to a statement Tuesday. That’s up from US$228.7 billion at the end of the first quarter, and beat company-compiled analyst estimates by a wide margin, which had anticipated assets under management to reach US$245.1 billion.

Asset growth over the six months through June was driven by US$19.8 billion in performance gains, as well as net inflows of US$7.1 billion, which were largely directed into long-only strategies, according to the statement. Analysts had expected US$1.6 billion in net flows over the period.

Shares in Man Group jumped as much as 9% in early London trading to reach 327.2p, the highest since 2010.

“In today’s markets, clients are consolidating their relationships with a smaller number of highly capable, strategic partners who can help them manage complex risk and growing macroeconomic uncertainty,” Man Group chief executive officer Robyn Grew said in the statement.

Man Group’s asset growth is the latest sign of the industry’s bumper first half. Hedge funds returned an average 7.4% in the six months through June, the best since 2009, according to data compiled by research firm PivotalPath.

See also: Mapletree launches first China logistics RMB fund with RMB1.5 bil portfolio, backed by China Life Capital

That’s whetting investor appetite, with giants including Singapore sovereign wealth fund GIC Pte and the Abu Dhabi Investment Council planning to allocate tens of billions between them to the industry.

“If you go beyond the numbers what is particularly pleasing is the broad-based nature of the growth you are seeing and the investment performance we are generating,” Man Group’s chief financial officer and chief operating officer Antoine Forterre said in an interview on Bloomberg Television. “Our main multistrat is up around 7.9% and that is the best representation of the alpha we have been able to generate for clients.”

London-based Man Group runs a range of investment products from hedge funds and quantitative money pools to long-only strategies. Last year, the investment firm began offering its first ETFs, with the launch of two actively managed bond funds.

See also: SoftBank’s US$40 bil loan for OpenAI stake gets 21 new lenders

Man Group was founded in 1783 by James Man as a barrel maker-cum-brokerage on Harp Lane, London. Over the next two centuries, it supplied rum to the Royal Navy and traded commodities such as coffee and sugar before eventually focusing exclusively on financial services.

title: AI boom propels Hong Kong exports to strongest growth since 1984
article:
(July 28): Hong Kong’s exports surged by the most in more than four decades to hit a record in June, fuelled by strong demand from the global boom in artificial intelligence.

The city’s outbound shipments last month soared by 53.4% from a year earlier, the largest increase since 1984, according to data released by the Census and Statistics Department on Monday. That brought the value of exports to a record high of HK$641.1 billion.

The gain exceeded all estimates in a Bloomberg survey of economists and followed a 40.8% expansion in May. Much of that spike was driven by demand for electronic products fuelled by the global buildout of AI infrastructure, with exports of electrical machinery and parts, data processing machines, and telecommunications equipment leading the increase, according to government data.

“Looking ahead, the robust demand for AI-related electronic products globally should render continued support to Hong Kong’s merchandise trade performance,” a government spokesperson said in a statement. “Yet, the recent re-escalation of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East deserves attention.”

Almost all of Hong Kong’s trade is driven by re-exports. The city produces little AI hardware itself but has become a vital conduit for high-tech goods moving in and out of China, emerging as a key node in the booming AI trade across Asia.

See also: Rising AI token costs not a problem for Toku, says CEO

In June, Hong Kong’s exports to Singapore jumped by 83%, followed by 80% to Taiwan and 59% to mainland China. Outside Asia, shipments to the US rose by 114%.

The Hong Kong Trade Development Council expects new US tariffs to have a limited impact on Hong Kong. Last week, the Trump administration imposed new tariffs of 12.5% on China, including Hong Kong, citing what it said were inadequate efforts to address forced labour. The new rates replace global duties of 10% that expired on July 24.

“While the tariff increase will affect Hong Kong’s exports to the US, it is worth noting that various exemptions remain in place, including for certain electronic products, which account for the majority of Hong Kong’s exports to the nation,” the council said in a press release.

See also: What comes next for Singapore as an AI hub?

Hong Kong’s imports, meanwhile, rose by 45.4% year-on-year in June, the strongest growth since 1992. Inbound shipments from South Korea surged by 177%, logging a fifth month of three-digit increases.

“On the whole, Hong Kong’s merchandise exports could see moderating growth momentum in the coming months, amid a likely gradual steadying of the technology upcycle, an easing global economy, as well as the high-base effect from last year,” said Bruce Pang, director of research at the Hong Kong Trade Development Council.
